content: This information does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. It is not intended to replace individualized medical advice and should not substitute for the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat a specific skin condition known as rosacea. It helps reduce the number of pimples and bumps on the face but may not significantly decrease redness. Although doxycycline belongs to the tetracycline class of antibiotics, it does not function as an antibiotic in this context because it does not inhibit bacterial growth. Do not use this product to treat infections, including viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Before starting this medication and each time you receive a refill, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, if available. Take this medication orally on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily in the morning. Swallow the capsules whole; do not crush or chew them. Take the medication with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise instructed. If stomach upset occurs, taking it with food or milk may help, but be aware that doxycycline may not work as effectively when taken with food, milk, or calcium-rich products. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (such as milk or yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it at the same time each day. Side Effects: Common side effects may include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, or mild headache. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, tetracycline drugs like doxycycline can cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension, or IH). Women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of IH are at greater risk. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping doxycycline, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections). Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking doxycycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to tetracycline or related drugs (such as minocycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Doxycycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). This medication may increase your sensitivity to the sun. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Children younger than 8 years old may be more sensitive to the side effects of doxycycline, particularly tooth discoloration. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using doxycycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Doxycycline may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated tetracycline-related drugs can result in serious illness. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
